content.text: Aga Khan University's Congenital Cardiac Programme - a multi-department collaboration - received the 2015 IQIC Improvement Science Award at the 11th Global Forum on Humanitarian Medicine in Cardiology and Cardiac Surgery held in Geneva from June 24-27, 2015.
The award was given in recognition of significant contributions to the care of paediatric cardiac surgery patients.
is a comprehensive congenital heart surgery database which aims at benchmarking data from developing countries to facilitate introspection and scope for improvement in outcomes at each centre.

Dr Babar Hasan, Associate Professor and Section Head, Paediatric Cardiology received the award on behalf of the University. AKU has been a member of IQIC since 2013 and is the only Pakistani centre to receive the award.

"This award recognises our efforts that have gone into developing one of the most comprehensive congenital cardiac programmes in Pakistan. This award is a reflection of the fact that AKU is being recognised as a national and regional leader in the field of congenital heart diseases," said Dr Hasan.

He further elaborated, "IQIC is not only a database but also provides learning resources to its members for combating morbidity and mortality in patients being operated for congenital heart disease. By following the best practices, AKU improved its infection control measures and successfully decreased morbidity and mortality rates in comparison with other member hospitals."

Globally cardiovascular diseases are the leading non-communicable diseases affecting developing countries. These international forums help to initiate a dialogue among various international partners to gather better knowledge concerning the needs of low income countries.

Dr Muneer Amanullah, Associate Professor, Cardiothoracic Surgery credited Aga Khan University's leadership and his team for this achievement. "We are grateful to the team for its support, especially Dr Nadeem Aslam, Assistant Professor and Paediatric Cardiologist and Amina Khan, Nurse Practitioner Congenital Cardiac Surgery. Their efforts made it possible to gather 100 per cent validated data which became the basis of the award. We hope that the Congenital Cardiac Programme is well under way to become the leading programme in the region," he said.
